A1.justification: Both readable, complete 27-page PDFs describe the same RIDER research, including Appendices A-E. Their text, equations, figures, tables and algorithms support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original RNA inverse-design experiments, including sequence recovery, structural similarity and AlphaFold3 validation. Appendix D contains original ablation and hyperparameter results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including the benchmark comparisons, cross-predictor validation and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1-3 retain the same GVP-GNN conditional diffusion model, DDIM sampling, advantage estimation, policy optimization and reward functions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RNASolo-derived dataset, 100-structure test set and 14-structure subset. No training or evaluation task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: RiboDiffusion, gRNAde, RIDE/Best-of-N and the ablation variants retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. The newly cited RL methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same splits, best-of-16 sequence-recovery evaluation at temperature 0.1, structural metrics, model configurations and training budgets.

E4.justification: The sequence-recovery correlation analysis, cross-predictor validation, structural examples, and advantage-estimation, reward-function and hyperparameter ablations are unchanged, including Appendix D.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 7 retain mean and standard deviation over five independent runs. Figures 7-9 and 13-15 retain SEM error bars, and the random-seed reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: The result tables and figures retain the same entries, values and findings. For example, Table 1 still reports RIDE NSR of 0.61 ± 0.02 and composite-reward RIDER GDT_TS of 0.62 ± 0.02.

T1.justification: The diffusion, policy-gradient and reward equations in Section 3, graph definitions in Appendix B, and structural-metric formulas in Appendix C are unchanged. No theoretical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty and performance claims concerning direct structural optimization, sequence recovery and structural-similarity improvements.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning sequence recovery, metric complementarity, generalization across predictors and training stability are unchanged. Appendix E retains the in silico limitation and proposed experimental validation.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B retain the same pseudocode, architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, memory requirements and training-time information. The project repository link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds eight RL works covering general decision-making, multi-agent learning, robotic control and Go. This broadens the background locally without changing RIDER's positioning relative to RNA-design or diffusion methods.

P1.justification: The RL background paragraph is locally rewritten and its heading shortened to 'Reinforcement learning'. Bibliographic formatting and metadata, the title's dash and report dates are revised; the overall narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded related-work paragraph slightly shifts subsequent text, and bibliography entries reflow across pages 11-14, substantially filling the previously sparse page 14. Figures 1-17, Tables 1-7 and algorithm displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies more explicit support for the RL background and fuller, more consistent bibliographic information, including publication details for RhoFold and RhoDesign. These provide a limited improvement in context and reference usability; the scientific evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged.
